pr_title: rank function returns int64 when float64 isn't necessary
pr_body:
- [ ] closes #55598
- [ ] [Tests added and passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#writing-tests) if fixing a bug or adding a new feature
- [ ] All [code checks passed](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#pre-commit).
- [ ] Added [type annotations](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/development/contributing_codebase.html#type-hints) to new arguments/methods/functions.
- [ ] Added an entry in the latest `doc/source/whatsnew/vX.X.X.rst` file if fixing a bug or adding a new feature.

Made a few small changes, makes it so when the parameter "method" is anything other than "average" and pct is false, the ranks returned are int64 instead of float64.

122 out of 564 tests failed due to this change, with the majority of cases the issue being:
E       Attribute "dtype" are different
E       [left]:  Int64
E       [right]: float64

That is expected due to the changes, and if this commit is in line with what was expected in the issue #55598 I can change those tests so that they pass.

issue_context.title: ENH: Allow rank to return int64 for numpy types when no missing values are present
issue_context.body:
```python
In [2]: import pandas as pd

In [3]: df = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 1, 1, 2, 2], 'b': [1,2 ,3, 4, 5]})

In [4]: df.groupby('a').rank(method='min')
Out[4]: 
     b
0  1.0
1  2.0
2  3.0
3  1.0
4  2.0

In [5]: df.rank()
Out[5]: 
     a    b
0  2.0  1.0
1  2.0  2.0
2  2.0  3.0
3  4.5  4.0
4  4.5  5.0
```

In these cases, it would be more natural to return int64 instead of float64
comments: Agreed in all cases except for `method='average'`. Here, the value may need to be float in the case of ties (e.g. `df['a']` in the example above). If we were to return integers in the case of no ties, this would be value-dependent behavior. I think we should therefore prefer to always return float.
@rhshadrach Just making sure: when you said we should always prefer to return float were you talking exclusively about the specific case of `method='average'` or about any call of the rank function?
Cool, I'll give this a shot. Appreciate the quick response!
Hey, I made what I think is what was expected, would you mind taking a look just to let me know if I'm in the right path so I can change the tests to reflect the changes? Thanks!

review_comments: This will convert e.g. float64 to Int64 I think, which we don't want. I also don't think you can do something like `result.astype("int64")` as you _will_ want e.g. Int64 input to remain Int64 output. I'd hazard a guess it'd be better for the change to be deeper than this, perhaps within `pandas._libs.groupby.group_rank` itself.
Sorry for the confusion, but I thought that converting float64 into Int64 in the specified case of `method != "average" and not pct` was what was described in the Issue. Is this assumption incorrect?
No problem - but I think we want `int64`, not `Int64`.

From the OP in the linked issue:

> In these cases, it would be more natural to return int64 instead of float64
This is unnecessarily duplicating code - both paths have `ranker(data)`. Also, avoid adding more `return` statements unless it helps the structure of the code.
Similar remarks here about the use of `convert_dtypes`.
This is calling Series.rank / DataFrame.rank, why is it necessary to convert the dtype here?

Maybe I've misinterpreted the issue description. In this example given by the issue reporter:

```
In [5]: df.rank()
Out[5]: 
     a    b
0  2.0  1.0
1  2.0  2.0
2  2.0  3.0
3  4.5  4.0
4  4.5  5.0
```

I thought that it was requested for column b in this case (and in analogous cases) to return int64, i.e.:

 ```
In [5]: df.rank()
Out[5]: 
     a    b
0  2.0   1
1  2.0   2
2  2.0   3
3  4.5   4
4  4.5   5
```

Was I wrong?

Also, I used `convert_dtypes()` because I read in the documentation in a use example that it converts float64 into int64 when relevant (e.g. 5.0 = 5), and I couldn't think of possible errors other than maybe `NaN` converting into `<NA>`.
